title: First hearing jazz as a child in the French Quarter
summary: Rose says he grew up hearing skiffle bands in the street, met Armand Hug at age seven, and lived at St. Louis and Dauphine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. What about, uh, what's the first time you ever remember hearing jazz, either on records or live or whatever?

Well, of course it had to be live, because I can't remember any time when I didn't hear jazz. There was no way that you could grow up in the French Quarter and not hear jazz, just walking around in the street. And, uh, especially I remember, uh, when I was a kid, there were so many skiffle bands playing in the streets, there were people to throw them coins, you know. And, uh, that was the sound. That was the, and of course I used to go down by the Fern Dance Hall and stand across the street and listen to the band playing for the Diamond Dance operation that they had going there. And that was when I first met Armand Hug. I was seven, he was fifteen. He was playing on the job, though.
So you were, uh, you were wandering around in the, uh, in the quarter. Where did you live in the corner?
On the corner of St. Louis and Dauphin. Sam Morgan might have been on your neighborhood.
Maybe, uh, although I wasn't aware of him. Yeah.
The very first thing I actually remembered as a dramatic incident was looking out the third story back window of the house and watching the French Opera burn.
